title: Lorsch Abbey | Sophie's World Travel Inspiration
content: # Lorsch Abbey (Day out Frankfurt). The last stretch, though 300 years through history, takes a mere 45 minutes on the Autobahn. World Heritage sites are prolific and close in south-western Germany. In the car park, I spot a woman on a bicycle. That’s Andrea Klitsche, welcoming me to Lorsch Abbey. I’m eager to go out to the site as soon as possible, but Andrea advises a walk through the visitor centre first. Not many buildings remain, so Lorsch Abbey is a site that asks a lot of your imagination. Walking around, it’s at first difficult to picture this as one of the most famous monasteries of its time. It was a proprietary abbey, meaning that it was built on private grounds by a feudal lord, who also appointed the religious personnel. So what is the function of a secular building in the middle of such holy surroundings? The Abbey and Altenmünster of Lorsch is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
